summary: Arkansas State Forestry Commission lookout 98 near Canfield, Lafayette County; a 1950 federal survey describes its 130-foot glass cab; listed as removed. No build date found.

facts.design: Glass-enclosed cab on a four-legged steel tower
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts lists it as removed; no source describes the site now

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey described the station and its 130-foot tower, so the tower was standing by then

evidence.supports: station 1-3/4 miles south of the village of Canfield
evidence.quote: THE STATION IS LOCATED 1-3/4 MILES SOUTH FROM THE VILLAGE
OF CANFIELD, 100 FEET EAST OF STATE ROUTE 29.

evidence.supports: glass-enclosed cab on a four-legged steel tower
evidence.quote: IT IS A GLASS ENCLOSED CAB, MOUNTED ON TOP OF A FOUR-LEGGED STEEL TOWER
AND HAS AN OVER ALL HEIGHT OF 130 FEET.
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1950 (RLE)
Lafayette County - Arkansas State Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: commission set up by Act 234 in 1931 and built many more towers
evidence.quote: The Arkansas Forestry Commission was established by Act 234 in 1931, and it too built many more towers.

evidence.supports: more than 120 fire towers at their height, 1930s to 1970s
evidence.quote: At the height of their use (1930s to 1970s), Arkansas had more than 120 fire towers

notes_for_editor: Only two sources. Two web searches found no other Canfield tower history; the Wikipedia Canfield page and Preserve Arkansas list had nothing on it. No build date, staffing, fires or access found. height_m 39.6 is converted from the 130-foot NGS figure (the brief had none). The NGS text is read through the Forest Lookouts page; no NGS datasheet was fetched directly.
